card.name: Animal names before Latin species names
card.fires_on: Words right before or inside a Latin genus or species name for an animal, such as 'family', an opening parenthesis after a common name, or partway through a genus name. Seen in dictionary entries and wildlife texts.

modes.label: Before Latin name
modes.description: A word like 'family' or '(' right before a Latin taxonomic name of an animal.
modes.example: Any hymenopterous insect of the<< family>> Ichneumonidæ,

modes.label: Inside genus names
modes.description: Partway through an animal's Latin genus name or common name.
modes.example: The Egyptian mongoose, Herpest<<es>> ichneumon, found in Africa

modes.label: Parenthesis after common name
modes.description: An opening bracket after an animal's common name, where the Latin name follows.

card.writes: It nudges the model toward fish and marine-life words (fish, scale, coral) and away from brick words.
card.plain: It fires where an animal's scientific Latin name is about to appear or is being spelled out, especially for mongooses, insects and fish.
